label: rare content-dependent firing near the delimiter in long sequences
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.04% of steps). Its timing is clear: about 77% of activation mass falls in the window from two steps before <DEL> to the first copy step (recall_idx 1, i.e. input = the first original token echoed back), and almost all of it in L = 8-9 sequences. It never fires at t < 3, and rarely in short sequences or late in the copy phase. Within that window, though, it fires on only about 0.3% of steps. Firing depends on sequence content in a way I could not capture: it is enriched for first tokens 2/c/1/l/w/q/z, for b or digits among the original tokens, and for out_tok 2. Conjunctions of these raise precision only to about 3% and cost recall. Activation is weakly larger inside the window (top-quartile coverage 0.86 versus 0.69 for the bottom quartile). No coherent monosemantic description was found; the predicate records the timing window only.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=c (+3.91), orig0=2 (+3.60), phase=2 & out_tok=2 (+3.56), phase=2 & in_tok=2 (+3.00), orig0=l (+2.96), in_tok=z (+2.94). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-3.85), orig1=n (-2.70), orig3=o (-2.56), orig2=q (-2.51).
